content: Theophylline is a medication prescribed to prevent and treat wheezing, shortness of breath, and difficulty breathing caused by asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and other lung diseases. It works by relaxing and opening the air passages in the lungs, making it easier to breathe. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Theophylline is available in various forms, including tablets, capsules, solutions, and syrups, and is taken orally. It is typically taken every 6, 8, 12, or 24 hours, depending on your doctor’s instructions. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take theophylline exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. It should be taken with a full glass of water on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal. Do not chew or crush extended-release tablets; swallow them whole. Some forms, such as Theo-Dur Sprinkles, can be swallowed whole or opened and mixed with soft food, but the contents should not be chewed. Theophylline helps control symptoms of asthma and other lung diseases but does not cure them. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Theophylline is sometimes used to treat breathing problems in premature infants. If this applies to your baby, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Before taking theophylline, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to theophylline or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription medications you are taking, especially allopurinol, azithromycin, carbamazepine, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, diuretics, erythromycin, lithium, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, propranolol, rifampin, tetracycline, or other medications for infections or heart disease. Also, inform them about any nonprescription medications, vitamins, or supplements you are taking, particularly those containing ephedrine, epinephrine, phenylephrine, phenylpropanolamine, or pseudoephedrine, as these can increase the side effects of theophylline. Avoid taking these medications without consulting your doctor. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had seizures, ulcers, heart disease, thyroid disorders, high blood pressure, liver disease, or a history of alcohol abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. If you become pregnant while taking theophylline, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, inform your doctor if you use tobacco products, as cigarette smoking can reduce the effectiveness of theophylline. While taking theophylline, avoid consuming large amounts of caffeine-containing foods and beverages, such as coffee, tea, cocoa, and chocolate, as they may increase the medication’s side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. If you experience severe shortness of breath, contact your doctor immediately. Theophylline may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, restlessness, insomnia, and irritability. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include vomiting, increased or rapid heart rate, irregular heartbeat, seizures, and skin rash. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store theophylline in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to theophylline. Do not switch brands of theophylline without consulting your doctor. Do not share your medication with others, and ask your pharmacist any questions about refilling your prescription.
